title: xterm 6.0 Terminal.dispose() leaks GC roots inside the library — fixable only by upstream bump, and minor bumps silently reshape the options surface
summary: xterm.js 6.0 instance pooling/hibernation (TerminalWebGLManager, terminalInstanceService): Terminal.dispose() fails to release internal GC roots when the WebGL addon is attached, so renderer heap grows across close/hibernate cycles despite correct app-side dispose ordering; the leak is upstream-only and invisible on DOM-renderer panes. Minor xterm bumps also silently reshape the options surface.

title: node-pty kill() leaks the master /dev/ptmx fd — every PTY teardown path must call destroy(), not just the pool
summary: node-pty's `TerminalProcess` PTY teardown (electron/services/pty/TerminalProcess.ts) leaks the master /dev/ptmx fd because `kill()` alone never releases it; all three live-process end-of-life paths (kill, onExit, dispose) must converge on `destroy()`, or fd churn exhausts macOS `ptmx_max` (~511) and blocks new terminal spawns.

title: Plugin subsystem integration traps: shared caches need ref-counting, dispatch needs the focused view, security pins must be purged on uninstall
summary: Plugin subsystem integration (`PluginService`/`WhenClauseService`/`plugin-mcp`) exhibits cross-plugin coupling traps invisible to per-PR review: process-global caches (compiled `when`-clause ASTs) need ref-counting before eviction, dispatch must target the focused view, and security pins must be purged on uninstall, else unloading one plugin breaks another or leaks registrations.

title: Atomic plugin install: extract to a SIBLING temp dir for same-filesystem rename, never re-throw in proper-lockfile onCompromised, restore runtime state on swap rollback
summary: PluginInstaller (`electron/services/plugin/PluginInstaller.ts`), the sole writer to `~/.daintree/plugins/`, must extract `.dntr` archives into a SIBLING temp dir rather than `os.tmpdir()` — otherwise the final `fs.rename` hits `EXDEV` across filesystem mounts and breaks atomicity; the swap also needs multi-instance lockfile guarding and runtime-state restoration on rollback.

title: Track the durable worktree restore target separately from the in-session active selection
summary: Worktree restore in the project-switch flow (`useWorktreeSelectionStore` snapshotted via `buildOutgoingState`, rehydrated by `stateHydration`) conflates the in-session active selection with the durable restore target, so transient worktrees from a batch PR-merge run get persisted and restored instead of the user's real root worktree.

title: React.lazy retry and AbortSignal teardown in the plugin view host: new lazy() ref per reset, ref-mirror the post-retry AbortController
summary: PluginViewHost (`src/components/Plugin/PluginViewHost.tsx`) plugin module retry/teardown: reusing the same React.lazy() ref after a load failure makes "Try again" silently reload the cached failed module, and not ref-mirroring the post-retry AbortController aborts a stale controller so the live plugin view's fetches/subscriptions leak past unload.

title: Sharing one React instance with externalized plugin bundles via host importmap
summary: Plugin view rendering (externalized React + host importmap): sharing the host's single React instance fails silently or at first render in three independent ways — a duplicate React copy slips into the plugin bundle, CSP strips the inline `<script type="importmap">`, or the HTML parser rejects the importmap tag — surfacing as `Invalid hook call`.

title: Custom Electron protocol containment needs realpath + O_NOFOLLOW-on-candidate, and privileged schemes must register before app.whenReady()
summary: Electron custom-scheme containment (`plugin://`/`daintree-file://` handlers in `electron/setup/protocols.ts`): lexical `path.relative` traversal checks pass while symlinked components escape the plugin root, so containment requires realpath plus O_NOFOLLOW on the candidate; privileged schemes also silently break unless registered via `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` before `app.whenReady()`.

title: Push-hydrated per-project WebContentsView goes stale after LRU eviction — needs init gate + targeted snapshot replay on view-ready
summary: Plugin contribution mirroring into per-project WebContentsViews relies on a mount-time IPC pull plus an EVENTS_PUSH listener; both fail intermittently when the pull races plugin startup activation (handlers return empty) or when LRU-evicted views cold-restore and remount before the next broadcast, leaving contributions silently empty until an unrelated mutation fires. Fix gates init and replays a targeted snapshot on view-ready.

title: Viewport-relative clamp belongs in a mount effect, not the zustand persist merge callback (innerWidth=0 pre-show)
summary: Portal dock width restore (zustand persist in src/store/portalStore.ts) clamps the persisted width against the viewport inside the persist merge callback, where window.innerWidth is still 0 pre-show, so safeMax collapses to PORTAL_MIN_WIDTH and every restore snaps to the floor; the viewport-relative clamp must run in a mount effect instead.

title: Native-module afterPack validation: N-API dlopen polarity is inverted from NAN, and existence checks pass on present-but-broken binaries
summary: afterPack native-module validation (scripts/afterPack.cjs) for vendored crash-safe PTY reapers: existence/X_OK checks pass on present-but-broken binaries (unresolved transitive deps, wrong arch), and N-API dlopen probe polarity is inverted from NAN while esbuild bundling instead of externalizing posix-pty-reaper breaks getSupervisorPath() resolution — so a dead reaper compiles, signs, and ships, failing only at first runtime use.

title: Stream interim transcription as a CodeMirror WidgetDecoration, not document text, to keep undo history clean
summary: HybridInputBar dictation streams interim speech-to-text deltas as CodeMirror document text via setDraftInput/doc.replace, so 30-50 volatile interim revisions per utterance pollute undo history (one Ctrl-Z reverts a mid-word interim, not the whole dictation) and cause visible churn; fix renders interim text as a WidgetDecoration instead. Related: sendFromEditor's final-transcript drop against the pre-stop doc (#9172).

title: Gate expensive GraphQL revalidation fan-out behind a cheap REST conditional-GET ETag probe; commit the ETag only when the caller is in sync, and keep polling CI on a 304
summary: PullRequestService steady-state PR poll fans out one ~3-point GraphQL re-fetch per tracked open PR, so at scale (25 PRs/30s) it overruns GitHub's 5000/hr GraphQL budget even on an idle repo; gate the fan-out behind a zero-cost REST conditional-GET ETag probe and only revalidate on a non-304.

title: VoiceOver drops aria-live updates from outside a focused aria-modal — close before announce, route via the announcer store
summary: ARIA-live announcer for destructive-confirm dialogs: closing an `aria-modal` element before announcing silently drops the `aria-live`/`document.ariaNotify` message on macOS VoiceOver, so blind users get no result feedback though the visible UI updates; announce before close.

title: Split PluginService load into scan-time vs activation-time; idempotent activatePlugin must never reject and must guard the unload race
summary: PluginService (electron/services/PluginService.ts) eagerly import()-ed and activate()-d every curated plugin's main module at startup, making cold-start cost scale linearly with the plugin set even for unused plugins; split loading into cheap scan-time contribution-point registration vs lazy activation, and make activatePlugin idempotent (never reject) while guarding the unload race.

title: Don't gate the crash stack trace behind import.meta.env.DEV — surface it in prod, scrubbed at the viewer boundary, scoped to stack only
summary: ErrorBoundary/ErrorFallback gated the "Technical details" stack trace behind import.meta.env.DEV, so production crash reports and the crash reporter shipped with zero trace — useless exactly where debugging is hardest. Surface the stack in prod too, scrubbed via reportScrubbers at the viewer boundary and scoped to the stack only.

title: macOS hardened-runtime entitlements rot across Electron majors; codesign --deep does not check per-Mach-O Team ID
summary: macOS release codesigning carries stale hardened-runtime entitlements in build/entitlements.mac.plist (e.g. allow-unsigned-executable-memory, unneeded since Electron 12) that survive major upgrades invisibly — they never fail builds, notarization, or runtime, only silently widen the security-relaxation surface; codesign --deep also skips per-Mach-O Team ID verification.

title: WebContentsView first-paint: inject skeleton CSS/JS on dom-ready not pre-loadURL, and thread projectId via additionalArguments not a URL query (preserves V8 bytecode cache)
summary: In ProjectViewManager's per-project WebContentsView cold-start path, inject first-paint skeleton CSS/JS on dom-ready rather than before loadURL (pre-loadURL injection is a silent no-op), and pass projectId via additionalArguments instead of a ?projectId= URL query, since query strings break V8 bytecode cache reuse across project switches.

title: VoiceOver drops aria-live updates outside the focused aria-modal subtree — use document.ariaNotify (Electron 41) with a co-located announcer fallback
summary: macOS VoiceOver silently drops aria-live announcements fired from the App-root AccessibilityAnnouncer while any aria-modal dialog is open — the DOM updates but nothing is spoken, with no error or failing test. Fix routes async status through Electron 41's document.ariaNotify with a co-located in-modal announcer fallback.

title: Hide a main-process WebContentsView by parking it offscreen (not removeChildView), and set its background before loadURL to kill the white flash
summary: PortalManager's main-process WebContentsView AI-host overlays: removeChildView destroys page state (scroll, streaming, WebSocket/SSE) on close/reopen, and missing setBackgroundColor before loadURL causes a white flash on first paint. Park the view offscreen instead of detaching, and set its background before loading.

title: Theme palette gates that constrain only OKLab L (lightness) leak chroma/hue drift — gate them warn-first, never hard-fail hand-tuned palettes
summary: Built-in theme palette test gates (`getSurfaceRampMetrics` ramp-monotonicity/ΔL-step assertions, OKLab accent-distinctness floor) that constrain only OKLab lightness silently leak chroma/hue drift, so retuning to pass them degrades hand-tuned theme identity (sidebar green tint, hue shifts); gate palettes warn-first, never hard-fail.

title: Batch multi-panel spawns at the store, not via Promise.all — Zustand's per-set() flush defeats React 19 auto-batching
summary: Multi-panel spawn batching (spawnPanelsFromRecipe, recipeStore.runRecipeWithResults): Zustand flushes synchronously per set() call, so each addPanel triggers its own React commit and CSS grid reflow — Promise.all does NOT collapse them past React 19 auto-batching. Batch all panelIds appends in a single store mutation.

title: insertCSS (user-origin) loses to renderer inline styles (author-origin); seed first-paint theme via webPreferences.additionalArguments → process.argv, not insertCSS
summary: Main-process first-paint theming via wc.insertCSS(cssOrigin:"user") loses the CSS cascade to the renderer's author-origin inline :root styles, so the wrong theme flashes on every cold start, project switch, and LRU view re-creation until async config resolves; seed the scheme through webPreferences.additionalArguments → process.argv instead.

title: Plugin unload cascade needs per-step try/catch — one throwing disposer strands later cleanup and leaks registry entries
summary: PluginService.unloadPlugin (electron/services/PluginService.ts) runs a teardown cascade across many registries without per-step try/catch, so one throwing disposer aborts later steps and leaks registry entries — notably orphaned *Impls entries that surface as duplicate-id errors on the plugin's next load; the renderer's plugin.invoke also swallows rejections, hiding throwing plugin actions.

title: Sliding-TTL security grants need a wall-clock ceiling from issuedAt or a caller can refresh them forever
summary: MCP server GrantCache "Approve once" grants use a sliding TTL: every dispatch calls refresh() to push expiresAt = now + 15min, so an agent calling the tool more often than the window never lets it expire — turning a one-shot approval into a permanent capability outliving its SSE session. Fix: clamp against a wall-clock ceiling derived from issuedAt.

title: Dev-server readiness needs a 5xx-warmup guard plus an HMR WebSocket handshake — HTTP 2xx alone is a false-ready
summary: DevPreviewReadinessProbe.waitForServerReady (electron/services/DevPreviewReadinessProbe.ts) treats any non-5xx HTTP response as ready, but 404/401/405 from history-fallback or warming auth proxies, and Docker port-forward 502/503/504 gateways that later resolve to 200, all yield false-ready panels pointed at error pages; even a clean 200 HTML shell can precede an HMR-handshake-ready bundler.

title: Every shell.openExternal must funnel through openExternalUrl's platform-conditional protocol allowlist — a renderer-supplied URL after a typeof check is a bypass
summary: Main-process shell.openExternal calls must route through the central openExternalUrl wrapper (electron/utils/openExternal.ts), which checks a URL against ALLOWED_PROTOCOLS; a renderer-supplied URL passed after only a `typeof === "string"` check (e.g. OAuth loopback authUrl) lets the renderer launch file:/javascript:/custom-scheme handlers via the OS, and every ad-hoc call site is its own unauditable bypass.

title: ready-to-show never gates first paint under WebContentsView-per-project — use appWebContents dom-ready, wired before loadURL
summary: Window first-paint under the WebContentsView-per-project architecture: because the React UI loads in a child `appView` rather than the BrowserWindow's own webContents, calling `win.show()` right after `loadURL()` reveals the window before the renderer paints, causing a blank-flash race; gate reveal on `appWebContents` dom-ready wired before `loadURL`, and don't let `DAINTREE_EARLY_RENDERER=0` mask it in E2E.

title: Strip E2E test backdoors from production builds via esbuild define + DCE
summary: Preload E2E backdoor bridges (`__DAINTREE_E2E_*` in `electron/preload.cts`) ship in packaged production builds because they gate only on a `process.env.DAINTREE_E2E_*` check, which is not a security boundary — any user launching the binary with the env var set unlocks IPC introspection and onboarding suppression; strip them at build time via esbuild `define` + dead-code elimination instead.

title: Stop processes holding a worktree directory open (dev server, terminals) BEFORE git worktree remove — Windows locks the dir
summary: Worktree deletion (`WorkspaceService.deleteWorktree` → `git worktree remove`) ignores independent main-process owners of the directory; a running `DevPreviewSessionService` dev server or open terminals hold an open handle, and on Windows the removal hard-fails (POSIX silently succeeds, masking it). Stop those processes before removal.

title: Vite-family dev servers ignore process.env.PORT — must inject --port via CLI flag, and --strictPort only on Vite/SvelteKit
summary: Dev Preview's DevPreviewCommandNormalizer mishandles Vite-family servers (Vite, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt): they ignore process.env.PORT and bind to framework defaults (5173/4321/3000), so the readiness poller hits the allocated URL and finds nothing — fix by injecting --port via CLI flag, adding --strictPort only for Vite/SvelteKit.

title: Dev-preview restart: a dead process does NOT free its TCP port — poll net.createServer().listen() before respawn (Windows TIME_WAIT)
summary: DevPreviewSessionService restart on Windows hits intermittent EADDRINUSE respawning on the same port because killing the dev-server PTY does not immediately release its TCP socket (TIME_WAIT), so the port lingers held; gate respawn on a net.createServer().listen() availability poll rather than process death.

title: xterm v6 screen-reader mode skips preventDefault on handled keys, so they bubble to Electron menu accelerators (F11/Tab passthrough)
summary: xterm v6 screen-reader (accessibility) mode in XtermAdapter's customKeyEventHandler returns true on handled keys without calling preventDefault, so bare accelerator keys (F11, Tab) bubble to Electron menu accelerators and Chromium focus traversal instead of emitting their PTY sequences on Linux/Windows; macOS escapes because its fullscreen accelerator is Ctrl+Cmd+F.

title: Wake suspended PTY processes with SIGCONT after SIGTERM so shutdown handlers run
summary: ProcessTreeKiller PTY teardown leaks dev-server ports and child workers when a descendant or shell was suspended via Ctrl+Z (SIGSTOP): a stopped process never delivers its SIGTERM/SIGHUP shutdown handler, so SIGCONT must precede SIGTERM to wake it before the sigkillSweep escalation.

title: Terminal panes must not intercept PTY-owned keys (Tab) for app navigation — it silently breaks shell/agent autocomplete
summary: xterm `customKeyEventHandler` in `XtermAdapter`: keys the PTY owns (Tab, Shift+Tab) must not be intercepted for app-level navigation. Routing them to `nav.focusRegion.next`/`prev` silently swallows the keys, breaking shell tab-completion, agent autocomplete, and TUI Tab handling with no error.

title: Per-project workspace-hosts each fire the same forge poll — arbitrate with a poll lease in MAIN, not the host
summary: Forge (GitHub) PR polling duplicates work when multiple windows watch one repo: each forks its own per-project workspace-host UtilityProcess, so N windows fire N identical GraphQL polls, multiplying API usage and rate-limit burn. Per-host `inFlightByArgs` dedup can't collapse sibling-host calls; arbitration requires a poll lease in main, not the host.

title: Provider-abstraction migration silently dropped per-query cache + dedup
summary: Routing all GitHub access through the new CodeForge provider abstraction (forgeProvider.runQuery + ForgeBridge over forge:rpc) silently dropped the per-entity 60s cache and singleflight dedup that lived in the replaced concrete service layer, so every poller/watcher/user call became an independent GraphQL round-trip, burning rate limit and multiplying cross-process IPC. When migrating to a provider interface, audit for caching/dedup that lived in the old layer, not just return-shape parity.

title: React 19 Suspense FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS (300ms) stacks additively with the 400ms animate-pulse-delayed CSS gate — never wire that skeleton as a Suspense fallback; loading placeholders also need a minimum-dwell floor
summary: React 19 Suspense skeleton gating in Daintree's anti-flicker loading system: the 300ms FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS stacks additively onto the 400ms `animate-pulse-delayed` CSS onset gate, so wiring that skeleton as a Suspense fallback yields a ~700ms blank dead-zone then a layout-shifting pop; separately, an onset-only gate flashes when work resolves just after it clears, so placeholders also need a minimum-dwell floor.

title: Panel focus suppression: use an explicit focusPolicy field, never overload spawnedBy provenance to encode focus intent
summary: panelStore.addPanel focus arbitration conflates two orthogonal axes — provenance (spawnedBy) and focus policy — into one field, forcing background callers like useAgentLauncher to mis-tag non-MCP spawns as "mcp" to inherit focus suppression; split intent into an explicit focusPolicy field instead.

title: dnd-kit CSS transform and framer-motion layout animation must live on separate DOM nodes (panel tab strip)
summary: Panel tab strip sortable buttons stutter on drag-end when dnd-kit's CSS transform and framer-motion's FLIP layout animation share a DOM node; `SortableTabButton`'s redundant inner `m.div layout="position"` fights the outer `m.div` from `PanelTabList`/`DockedTabGroup`. Keep transform and layout animation on separate nodes.

title: role=group section headers inside a listbox break under Chromium 146 + VoiceOver — use aria-disabled option separators instead
summary: Command palette listbox section headers (`ActionPalette`/`SearchablePalette`) are inaccessible under Chromium 146 + VoiceOver: `role="presentation"` headers leave sections unannounced, while the spec-recommended `role="group"` + `aria-label` fix drops the accessible name and announces "empty group"; use `aria-disabled` option separators instead.

title: Defensive pointer/key suppression on xterm panes silently breaks screen-reader cursor routing and shell Tab-completion
summary: xterm terminal panes: defensive event suppression breaks assistive tech — unfocused-pane pointerdown suppression (`stopPropagation`/`setPointerCapture`) swallows screen-reader cursor-routing clicks, and intercepting Tab/Shift+Tab in the xterm key handler to escape the focus trap breaks shell and agent Tab-completion in every pane.

title: Tier-gated hibernation needs an explicit re-arm hook when a non-tier policy input changes (same-tier no-op trap)
summary: TerminalInstanceService hibernation arms a one-shot eligibility timer on tier-drop to BACKGROUND that waits out the full AGENT_IDLE_SILENCE_MS; later non-tier policy changes (user-backgrounding a panel) hit a same-tier no-op and never re-arm, so the new bypass can't shorten the wait and memory isn't reclaimed early.

title: Chromium aria-live regions: keep the node always-mounted and commit the cleared state in its own rAF frame, or announcements silently drop
summary: Chromium accessibility-tree commit model silently drops `aria-live`/`role="status"` announcements (ShortcutHint, VoiceRecordingAnnouncer, dnd-kit drag) when the region unmounts or its cleared state isn't committed in a separate rAF frame; markup-level tests pass while VoiceOver/NVDA speak nothing or double-announce.

title: Floating UI autoUpdate never observes the collision boundary — bump a data-* attr (not key=) to reposition open popovers when a WebContentsView panel resizes the boundary
summary: Radix Popover/Floating UI's `autoUpdate` tracks the trigger and floating elements but never re-measures the `collisionBoundary` element, so an open popover keeps stale placement when a `WebContentsView` panel toggle resizes the `--right-obstruction-offset` boundary div; force a reposition by mutating a `data-*` attr on `PopoverContent` rather than remounting via `key=`.

title: Bulk terminal startup needs admission backpressure (one xterm/PTY attach at a time), not post-burst WebGL repaint
summary: Bulk terminal startup (`addPanel` optimistic commit + `XtermInstanceService`/WebGL attach): committing and mounting every panel in one grid layout pass overwhelms Chromium's render lifecycle and xterm open/attach/fit, causing blank/stalled panes; fix needs per-attach admission backpressure, not post-burst WebGL repaint, which can't recover the overloaded frame.

title: Utility processes have no plugin loader — registry-dependent host logic fails silently; bridge to main via RPC
summary: Workspace-host `UtilityProcess` (workspace-host.ts) runs no plugin loader, so forge-registry lookups in `PullRequestService` resolve to nothing — `findPRByBranch` is skipped every poll with only a debug log, leaving worktree-sidebar PR rows silently empty. Bridge registry-dependent host logic to main via RPC.

title: Filtering focus reports from input is not enough — the agent's delayed repaint outlives the echo window and promotes idle→busy via a second output path
summary: ActivityMonitor classifies agent terminals idle/busy from PTY output; DEC mode ?1004 focus reports (CSI I/O) have two paths, so filtering them from input detection alone misses the output path — the agent's delayed repaint after a focus event arrives past the echo window and falsely promotes idle→working.

title: A manual Rolldown chunk group re-bundles lazy-imported code back into the eager closure, defeating LazyMotion deferral
summary: Rolldown's manualChunks/chunk-grouping in the Vite build pulls lazy `import()`-ed modules (framer-motion `domMax` via `motionFeatures.ts`) back into the eager first-paint chunk, silently defeating LazyMotion deferral while the first-render chunk-budget script reports no movement, hiding the regression from CI.

title: Rolldown lazyBarrel prunes nothing without a package.json sideEffects allowlist
summary: Rolldown's `lazyBarrel` (Vite 8 renderer build) silently prunes nothing unless `package.json` declares a `sideEffects` allowlist; absent it, barrel files like `src/hooks` pull every re-exported module into the eager startup graph, and no byte-budget gate catches the regression.

title: Module-scope app:boot promise read via React 19 use() must reset on HMR and annotate the thenable for synchronous reads
summary: React 19 module-scope `use()` boot promise (`src/lib/bootPromise.ts`, fired at module-eval in `main.tsx`) caches a resolved `app:boot` payload that outlives the V8 context, so Vite HMR re-eval or dev context reuse silently serves stale boot data; the module-eval call also runs before any React error boundary or `bootstrap().catch()` exists, requiring HMR reset plus a synchronously-annotated thenable.

title: Occluded incoming WebContentsView stalls the cold-switch paint gate — unfreeze it after did-finish-load to keep rAF firing
summary: ProjectViewManager cold-switch paint gate: occluding the incoming WebContentsView behind the outgoing view via addChildView(view,0) starves its rAF loop, so APP_VIEW_PAINTED never fires and switches fall back to the high soft/hard timeouts; unfreeze the view after did-finish-load to keep rAF running.

title: Utility-host bootstraps must install error handlers BEFORE the dynamic import(); post-Electron-37 a native-load failure only warns and silently hangs waitForReady
summary: Utility-host bootstraps (`pty-host`/`workspace-host`) install `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` handlers inside the host module that only loads via `await import()`; post-Electron-37 a native dlopen failure (node-pty `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`, better-sqlite3, @parcel/watcher) merely warns, so the host never evaluates, never posts `ready`, and the parent's `waitForReady()` hangs the app silently on startup.

title: Executable image path is a setproctitle-proof agent identity signal — but a shared per-PID probe needs explicit PID-reuse eviction
summary: ProcessDetector agent-identity detection (electron/services/ProcessDetector): when CLIs rewrite process.title via setproctitle and node-hosted agents blank comm/argv, comm- and argv-based matching mis-identifies the agent; resolving the PID's on-disk exe image path (ImagePathProbe) is tamper-proof, but a per-PID cache needs explicit PID-reuse eviction.

title: POSIX crash-safe PTY reaping needs a pipe-EOF supervisor sidecar — there is no Job Object analog
summary: HelpSessionJobService crash-safe PTY reaping silently no-ops on macOS/Linux: the original binding.gyp emitted zero non-Windows targets and the wrapper returned false, so no pipe-EOF supervisor sidecar reaps orphaned help-session PTY trees after a hard Electron crash, despite the feature being framed as cross-platform parity with Windows Job Objects.

title: Surviving utility-host crashes for fire-and-forget mutations needs a renderer outbox keyed by mutationId + epoch-scoped ack map echoed in every snapshot
summary: Workspace-host worktree-delete recovery: fire-and-forget MessagePort mutations are silently lost when the per-project utility host crashes mid-delete, and naive replay re-fires already-completed deletes against gone monitors, throwing spurious "Worktree not found" errors. Fix needs a renderer outbox keyed by mutationId plus an epoch-scoped ack map echoed in every snapshot.

title: Agent-state detection that diffs a visible-line snapshot is grid-geometry-dependent — add a viewport-independent OSC 9;4 heartbeat parsed from the raw PTY stream
summary: ActivityMonitor's `simpleOutputState` path detects agent "working" by diffing successive `getVisibleLines(n)` snapshots, making it grid-geometry-dependent: in a small grid tile the viewport exposes too few lines, so output streaming below the fold never changes the snapshot, starving the detector and firing a false idle after IDLE_DEBOUNCE_MS. Fix parses a viewport-independent OSC 9;4 heartbeat from the raw PTY stream.

title: Persisted JSON state: guard number fields with Number.isFinite (1e309 → Infinity → null) and quarantine corrupt files instead of silently resetting
summary: CrashLoopGuardService persists crash-loop-state.json validated only by typeof "number", so an overflow literal like 1e309 parses as Infinity, passes validation, poisons arithmetic, and JSON.stringify serializes it back to null — self-corrupting the file; guard numerics with Number.isFinite and quarantine corrupt files instead of silently resetting to fresh state and destroying forensic evidence.

title: errno .code is stripped on the plain typedHandle IPC path — the wrapError envelope is opt-in, not universal
summary: Electron IPC's `typedHandle` path serializes rejections as plain `Error` and strips custom properties like errno `.code` (EPIPE/EBADF) unless wrapped in the opt-in `wrapError` envelope; structured-clone drops the field, so renderer-side classifiers reading `err.code` silently see undefined.

title: Crash-recovery marker consumption must preserve-before-delete and be idempotent — recovery code that isn't itself crash-safe erases its own evidence
summary: CrashRecoveryService marker consumption in Electron main: deleting the `running.lock` marker before durably persisting the `session-state.json` backup (and relying on an in-memory snapshot) leaves a window where a SIGKILL/OOM/force-quit during the recovery path itself erases crash evidence and lets the new session's first backup tick clobber the live backup; preserve-before-delete and make consumption idempotent.

title: Destructive confirm must gate on the resolved per-target fan-out, not the source draft — snapshot it to avoid TOCTOU
summary: Fleet broadcast confirm gate (`needsFleetBroadcastConfirmation`, `src/components/Fleet/fleetBroadcast.ts`) evaluates the source editor draft instead of the per-target resolved bytes, so recipe-variable substitution can expand a safe draft past the 512-byte threshold or inject `rm -rf` after the check — a TOCTOU gap that bypasses the dialog or makes users approve a description rather than the bytes each pane receives. Snapshot the resolved fan-out and gate on that.

title: Electron 37+ utility-process hosts only WARN on unhandledRejection — fatal handlers must setImmediate(process.exit(1)) or the host zombies and supervision never fires
summary: Utility-process (pty-host/workspace-host) fatal error handlers must end with setImmediate(() => process.exit(1)) because Electron 37+ only warns (not crashes) on unhandledRejection, leaving a zombie host the parent never recycles.

title: ResourceGovernor flap: raw V8 heapUsed is a pre-GC sawtooth — threshold logic needs EMA + warmup + re-engage cooldown, and the blind timeout force-resume is half the loop
summary: ResourceGovernor (pty-host utility process) flaps under sustained memory pressure: raw V8 heapUsed is a pre-GC sawtooth, so threshold checks need an EMA plus warmup and re-engage cooldown, and the 10s blind force-resume timeout that ignores current utilization re-pauses PTYs in a ~12s pause/resume cycle.

title: app:// protocol V8 code cache won't persist without HTTP-cacheable response headers (Cache-Control + validator + 304)
summary: Electron's `app://` custom-protocol V8 code cache (`electron/setup/protocols.ts`, `electron/utils/appProtocol.ts`) silently never persists despite `codeCache: true` and `v8CacheOptions: "code"`; Chromium gates code-cache storage on HTTP-cacheable responses, so the handler must emit `Cache-Control`, a validator (ETag/Last-Modified), and honor conditional 304 requests.

title: app.getAppMetrics() privateBytes is Windows-only and returns 0 (not undefined) on macOS/Linux — `?? workingSetSize` never fires
summary: ProcessMemoryMonitor and ResourceProfileService read per-process memory via `proc.memory.privateBytes ?? workingSetSize`, but `app.getAppMetrics()` returns privateBytes as 0 (not undefined) on macOS/Linux, so the nullish fallback never fires and every process reads as zero memory — efficiency-profile escalation never triggers. Tests masked it by supplying populated privateBytes.

title: WebContents.setBackgroundThrottling is window-wide, not per-view — use CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate for per-renderer throttling
summary: ProjectViewManager throttles cached WebContentsView project views by calling WebContents.setBackgroundThrottling per view, but that flag is window-wide and a silent no-op for individual hidden views, so deactivated renderers keep burning CPU; per-renderer throttling requires CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate.

title: Don't dispose global singletons on last-window-close — macOS dock reactivation races the async teardown; move disposals to before-quit
summary: Global main-process singleton lifecycle in `setupWindowServices` (`electron/window/windowServices.ts`): disposing singletons on last-window-close races macOS dock reactivation, which re-enters init while async teardown is in flight and skips re-init because the `globalServicesInitialized` guard reads stale `true`, leaving new windows bound to half-torn-down PtyClient/WorkspaceClient. Move disposals to `before-quit`.

title: Don't subscribe to a churning map (panelsById) even under useShallow — split membership (reactive ID list) from materialization (non-reactive getState in an ID-gated memo)
summary: `useContentGridContext` re-runs the entire terminal-grid derivation on every agent state/activity tick because it subscribes to the churning `panelsById` map (even via `useShallow`); fix by subscribing only to a reactive panel-ID list for membership and materializing panel objects via non-reactive `getState()` inside an ID-gated memo.

title: Coalesce high-frequency panel-store writes through a shared rAF buffer, but keep ordered/side-effecting agent-state writes direct
summary: usePanelStore subscriber-notify amplification: Zustand 5 runs its synchronous subscriber/selector pass on every setState, so per-event activity and flow-status writes from src/store/listeners/panel/ scale linearly with agent count, causing redundant selector runs and re-render churn decoupled from frames actually painted; coalesce high-frequency writes through a shared rAF buffer while keeping ordered/side-effecting agent-state writes direct.

title: Don't hand-maintain a React.memo comparator over a fat object prop — pass the id and subscribe by id with useShallow so the selector IS the single field list
summary: React.memo over fat object props (GridPanel/GridTabGroup content-grid cells): a hand-written field-by-field comparator duplicates the field list that buildPanelProps consumes and silently drifts, leaving panel chrome stale on un-tracked field changes; pass the id and subscribe by id with useShallow so the selector is the single field list.

title: WindowRegistry primary must track browser-window-focus, not Map insertion order — register-time isFocused() promotion + focus-history unregister fallback
summary: WindowRegistry.getPrimary() (electron/window/WindowRegistry.ts) returns the first-opened window instead of the focused one because it relies on Map insertion order rather than browser-window focus; the bug is invisible in single-window sessions and only surfaces once a second window opens, misrouting notification clicks, recovery prompts, and theme application.

title: Module-level ProjectViewManager singleton (windowRef.ts) silently controls only the last-created window — fan all-window controls through WindowRegistry.all()
summary: ResourceProfileService memory-pressure controls (cached-view clamp, efficiency freeze, low-memory floor) reach ProjectViewManager via a module-level `windowRef.ts` singleton that tracks only the last-created window, so in multi-window sessions every window except the most recent keeps full cached-view limits and stays unfrozen under pressure; fan all-window operations through `WindowRegistry.all()`.

title: contextBridge strips Error own-properties a SECOND time after IPC — custom fields must be message-prefix encoded, not just envelope-serialized
summary: Electron `contextBridge` re-strips Error own-properties on the renderer side after IPC, so custom discriminant fields (e.g. `GitOperationError.leaseSha`, `gitReason`) survive the structured-clone envelope but vanish silently across the bridge; message/stack still arrive, so the loss surfaces as degraded behavior (force-push-with-lease falls back to plain force push) with no exception. Fields must be message-prefix encoded, not just envelope-serialized.

title: ProjectStore.setCurrentProject mutates persisted rows silently — every switch path must broadcast project:updated or cached WebContentsViews keep stale lastOpened and MRU jumps wrong
summary: ProjectStore MRU project switching under WebContentsView-per-project: setCurrentProject mutates persisted lastOpened only in-process, so switch paths that skip broadcasting project:updated leave other cached V8 views with stale timestamps, ranking the MRU sort wrong and highlighting the wrong default in the switcher palette.

title: Auto-respawn supervisors: a restart counter reset on 'ready' never trips in a crash-boot-crash loop — use a lazily-pruned sliding window of crash timestamps
summary: Process supervisor restart-cap logic (WorkspaceHostProcess/PtyHostLifecycle) miscounts when a counter resets on the `ready` event: a crash-boot-`ready`-crash loop zeroes the tally each cycle, so the give-up cap never trips and the host respawns forever without ever surfacing the `host-crash` recovery banner. Track crashes in a lazily-pruned sliding window of timestamps instead.

title: The renderer xterm buffer is an agent input source — never terminal.write() operational diagnostics into it
summary: TerminalScrollbackController.reduceScrollback in the renderer emits operational diagnostics via terminal.write() into the xterm buffer, but buffer.active is read back as agent context input — so any injected notice (e.g. the "[Daintree] Scrollback reduced" line) leaks into agent transcripts as fake program output, polluting model context every loop.

title: A @parcel/watcher topology watcher cannot report deletion of its own watched dir — gate the safety-net reconcile independently of the watcher
summary: WorkspaceService's @parcel/watcher topology watcher on `.git/worktrees/` cannot observe deletion of its own watched directory, so removing the last worktree emits no event or error and leaves a phantom sidebar row until the slow adaptive background poll happens to reconcile; gate the safety-net reconcile independently of the watcher.

title: MCP tools/list cost is re-paid every model turn — gate the manifest with mcpVisibility + actions.search/getSchema, not one big list
summary: MCP server's `tools/list` handler (`sessionServer.ts`) emits all ~300 Actions-registry entries with full input/output schemas (~200KB) per response; because the MCP protocol re-sends the active tool manifest as context every model turn, that schema cost is re-paid each turn instead of once, inflating per-turn tokens — fix by gating the manifest with mcpVisibility plus actions.search/getSchema lookup tools.

title: Idle/expiry setTimeout fires wrong across suspend/resume — anchor to awake-elapsed via SystemSleepService.getAwakeTimeSince, recompute on wake, re-check in the callback
summary: MCP-server session expiry timers (`SessionStore.createIdleTimer`/`createHttpIdleTimer`, `electron/services/mcp-server/sessionStore.ts`) use bare `setTimeout`, which doesn't track real elapsed time across laptop suspend/resume — so timers fire early (revoking active grants) or late (sessions linger); anchor to awake-elapsed via `SystemSleepService.getAwakeTimeSince`, recompute on wake, and re-check in the callback.

title: MCP tool approval must mint a per-(session,toolId) time-bounded grant, never elevate the whole session for its lifetime
summary: MCP tool-approval flow in `sessionServer.ts`: the "Approve once" path called `setSessionTier`, permanently elevating the whole help-session's tier and granting unbounded access to every tool at or below it; fix mints a per-(session,toolId) time-bounded grant instead. Standing-elevation/request-fatigue anti-pattern.

title: Virtualizing a dnd-kit sortable list unmounts the dragged source row mid-drag — snapshot active.data.current at drag-start or the drop silently cancels
summary: dnd-kit sortable rows inside a react-virtuoso virtualized list lose `active.data.current` when autoscroll pushes the dragged source row out of the overscan window, unmounting it and silently converting the drop into a cancel; snapshot the drag payload at drag-start (`onDragStart`) so reorder survives source-row unmount.

title: Project switch: forward-fail instead of PTY-only rollback once store/git-cache/log/context already committed; the production view-swap path never emitted PROJECT_ON_SWITCH
summary: Project-switch rollback in `ProjectSwitchService.performSwitch` only reverts the PTY mapping while the store, git cache, log buffer, and context tracker stay committed to the new project, leaving worse-than-failure state; the production `ProjectViewManager` swap path never emitted `PROJECT_ON_SWITCH`, so worktree-load errors were invisible.

title: Runtime destructive-tier escalation: keep danger:safe for MRU, gate with nonRepeatable + a pending-store to avoid the dock-collapse race
summary: Portal close-all actions (`portal.closeAllTabs`/`closeOthers`) are safe at 1-2 tabs but destructive at 3+; static `danger` metadata only encodes the worst case, so marking them `confirm` strips them from the action-palette MRU/Favorites rail and `repeatLast`. Keep `danger:"safe"`, gate the bulk case with runtime `nonRepeatable` plus a pending-store to dodge the dock-collapse race.

title: Post-switch renderer actions must hop through a main-process one-shot intent, gated on paint AND hydration separately
summary: ProjectViewManager per-project WebContentsView switching tears down the initiating renderer's V8 context, so any same-renderer continuation after switchProject never runs; the cross-view focus continuation must hop through a main-process one-shot intent gated separately on paint AND panelStore hydration, since paint fires while panelIds is still empty and dispatching agent.focusNextWaiting then silently no-ops.

title: Renderer-minted version counters can't see a host-process restart — mint (epoch, seq) at the authoritative writer and let a new epoch always win
summary: Worktree view-store version guard (`createWorktreeStore.ts`) mints monotonic counters in the renderer, so a `workspace-host` process crash/restart is invisible: post-restart re-hydration events aren't strictly newer than the climbing local counter and get silently dropped, stranding stale state. Fix mints (epoch, seq) at the authoritative writer so a new epoch always wins.

title: Self-induced file-watcher events: key a pending set by identity, never a blanket time-window suppressor
summary: WorkspaceService's `.git/worktrees/` watcher (workspace-host) uses a blanket time-window suppressor to skip reconcile after app-owned `git worktree add/remove`, but a wall-clock `suppressUntil` window can't distinguish self-induced events from concurrent external ones, so external removals during the window are silently dropped until the next adaptive poll; key suppression by per-operation identity instead.

title: Carry renderer-side terminal signals as a private-use OSC sequence, and defer the resulting xterm.write via queueMicrotask to escape parse reentrancy
summary: Terminal data-loss markers in TerminalInstanceService/TerminalParserHandler: writing styled ANSI text directly into the xterm buffer couples wire format to presentation, so the gap byte-count/reason are unreadable in WebGL-disabled E2E and any appearance tweak silently changes the transport; carry the signal as a private-use OSC sequence instead.

title: PortBatcher zero-copy flush: prove a chunk escaped node-pty's slab before transferring, and instrument the GC cost a buffer pool would retire before building one
summary: PortBatcher (electron/pty-host/portBatcher.ts) always allocates and copies a fresh Uint8Array on every PTY flush, even single-chunk flushes, because #4639's "never transfer node-pty's slab-backed Buffer.buffer" rule makes direct zero-copy transfer seem categorically unsafe; the trap is reaching for a buffer-pool/arena fix before proving a chunk has escaped the shared 8KB slab or measuring the GC cost the pool would actually retire.

title: Backgrounded terminals must hold incoming bytes in-queue, not parse them into xterm — gate every drain entry point and bump a wake generation to block stale-wake flushes
summary: TerminalOutputIngestService (renderer) keeps parsing in-flight MessagePort PTY batches into hidden xterm instances after a pane is backgrounded, since pty-host throttling only slows polling rather than suppressing it; xterm.write() then burns main-thread CPU parsing ANSI for unseen panes. Fix gates every drain entry point and bumps a wake generation to discard stale-wake flushes.

title: MCP tier allowlists typed as readonly string[] silently retain stale action IDs after a rename — const-satisfy BuiltInActionId to make drift a compile error
summary: MCP tier-authorization allowlists (`helpAssistantTierAllowlists.ts`, mcp-server `shared.ts`) typed as `readonly string[]` and wrapped in `Set<string>` silently retain stale action IDs after a registry rename — no build break, so the renamed action drops out of its privilege tier while the dead string matches nothing; const-satisfy `BuiltInActionId` to turn drift into a compile error.

title: Forensic ring buffers (crash breadcrumbs) need priority-aware eviction, not FIFO — noise displaces the entries that matter during the pre-crash burst
summary: ActionBreadcrumbService's main-process forensic ring buffer (MAX_RING=50) uses single-tier FIFO eviction, so chatty low-signal actions like repeated terminal.list spaced beyond the 250ms dedup window evict high-value danger-tier and error breadcrumbs during the pre-crash burst — invisible under steady load, manifesting only when forensic data matters most. Fix with priority-aware eviction.

title: Keybinding actionIds need a two-tier type split plus warn-and-drop on persisted user overrides
summary: KeybindingService applies the #4489 open-union ActionId uniformly to KeybindingConfig.actionId, so default-keybinding typos compile silently and surface only at runtime, and loadOverrides() persists user bindings for renamed/removed actions (e.g. app.toggleSidebar→nav.toggleSidebar) as dead entries; fix splits into a closed type for defaults plus warn-and-drop on unknown persisted overrides.

title: Plugin-contributed action danger must be host-derived from manifest capabilities, never trusted from the plugin's self-declaration
summary: Plugin system: a plugin's self-declared action danger is advisory only — the host (PluginService) derives the authoritative effectiveDanger from manifest.capabilities (CONFIRM_TRIGGERING_CAPABILITIES + compound-capability lattice), raise-only, with the renderer failing safe to "confirm" on a missing field.

title: executeJavaScript hangs on a CDP-frozen webview — read state via Page.getLayoutMetrics instead
summary: When a docked-but-inactive dev-preview/browser panel is CDP-frozen via useWebviewThrottle's Page.setWebLifecycleState, calling executeJavaScript (e.g. DevPreviewPane's window.scrollY capture) hangs forever; if eviction blanks src to about:blank mid-await the scroll position is silently lost. Read state through Page.getLayoutMetrics instead.

title: Dev-preview readiness: 5xx is a compiling shell (not ready), stdout markers fast-path the poll, and error detection must abort the in-flight poll
summary: Dev Preview readiness probe (DevPreviewReadinessProbe.ts): an HTTP 500 from a still-compiling Next.js dev server is a not-ready shell, so accepting any 100-599 status flips the session to running and renders an error page as success; also, detecting a dev-server error in handleData must abort the in-flight readiness poll, or a slow HEAD that later succeeds overwrites the error state.

title: Persisted-settings decode must be a total function that quarantines corrupt/future-version files instead of falling back to empty defaults; reject caller-supplied _schemaVersion at the IPC gate
summary: ProjectSettings persistence (electron/services/projectSettingsCodec.ts): a try/catch-to-empty-defaults decode is a data-loss trap — transient corruption or a newer-version file silently reverts to defaults, then the next save overwrites the original on disk. Decode must be total: quarantine corrupt/future-version files instead of falling back, and reject caller-supplied _schemaVersion at the project:save-settings IPC gate.

title: Built-in plugin singletons must share one esbuild chunk with main, and load from the chunk's own dir — else duplicate instances / silent registration gaps
summary: Runtime-loaded built-in plugins (e.g. github's GitHubAuth/rate-limit/token-health singletons via ForgeProviderImpl) must share one esbuild chunk with the main bundle and load from the chunk's own dir; a separate bundle inlines duplicate singleton copies, so IPC mutates one instance while the forge provider reads another and state silently diverges.

title: xterm attachCustomKeyEventHandler returning false bypasses onKey/onData — duplicate any listener side-effects (notifyEnterPressed) in the custom handler
summary: In xterm.js, an attachCustomKeyEventHandler that returns false short-circuits the event so onKey/onData listeners never fire — any side-effect wired there (e.g. notifyEnterPressed driving the directing→working agent-state transition) must be duplicated inside the custom handler, or it silently stops while the keystroke still reaches the PTY.

title: Dock popover dismissal guard: match a self-stamped attribute, not Radix-internal selectors, and re-provide its context across every createPortal boundary
summary: Radix Popover dock-dismissal guard (handleDockInteractOutside in dockPopoverGuard.ts) matched click targets against the global Radix-internal selector [data-radix-popper-content-wrapper], so any unrelated overlay anywhere in the document suppressed dismissal and any upstream Radix rename silently broke the guard. Fix: match a self-stamped data attribute and re-provide its context across each createPortal boundary.

title: Write-burst refresh tier: extend a deadline timestamp + single self-rearming timer, never per-write clearTimeout/setTimeout
summary: Driving xterm's BURST refresh tier from real PTY-write activity (TerminalWriteController/onPtyWrite) must extend a deadline timestamp checked by one self-rearming timer; per-write clearTimeout/setTimeout decay-resets jank Chromium 146's timer queue under 60fps+ output floods (hundreds of timer churns/sec). Also: BURST should reflect activity, not focus, since focus-derived BURST feeds wrong input to isWebGLEligibleTier and pool-pressure eviction.

title: Native disabled kills tooltip hover in Chromium 146 — use aria-disabled + click-gating, and Radix triggers open on pointerDown/keyDown not click
summary: In Chromium 146, native `disabled` suppresses pointer events so a Radix Tooltip-wrapped button never fires hover and its explanatory tooltip (why the control is blocked) is undiscoverable; use `aria-disabled` plus click/handler-gating instead, and remember Radix tooltip/dropdown triggers open on pointerDown/keyDown rather than click.

title: React 19 Activity hidden mode + Radix portaled overlays: portaled content escapes display:none and strands at (0,0)
summary: React 19 Activity mode="hidden" (used by FixedDropdown keepMounted) applies display:none, but Radix-portaled children like Tooltip render outside that subtree and so escape the hide, stranding fully-painted ghost overlays at (0,0) after the dropdown closes. Close/unmount portaled overlays explicitly rather than relying on Activity to hide them.

title: Off-Mac keybinding conflict detection must fold Cmd into Ctrl (same physical key) and early-return on AltGr
summary: KeybindingService conflict detection (findConflicts/registerBinding) and matchesEvent must treat Cmd and Ctrl as the same physical key off-Mac, or case-folded string compare silently misses collisions (e.g. Ctrl+Shift+E shadowing Cmd+Shift+E); also early-return on AltGr (ctrlKey && altKey) so international layouts don't false-match Ctrl combos.

title: Agent command-launch runs as shell startup args (PowerShell -EncodedCommand / cmd /K), and shell identity for quoting must NOT leak into spawn options or it kills the PTY pool
summary: In the terminal spawn handler (electron/ipc/handlers/terminal/lifecycle.ts, commandLaunch.ts buildCommandLaunchShell), launch agent commands as shell startup args (PowerShell -EncodedCommand / cmd /K) rather than echoing into the PTY or passing raw argv, since node-pty's Windows agent re-joins argv for CreateProcess and PowerShell/cmd re-parse quoting/backslashes differently, breaking paths with spaces or quotes. Keep shell-identity quoting state out of spawn options or it corrupts the PTY pool.

title: Windows console UTF-8 needs in-band shell startup args, not LANG — per-shell mechanism in getDefaultShellArgs
summary: Windows console UTF-8 in PTY shells (`getDefaultShellArgs`, `terminalShell.ts`) requires per-shell in-band startup args (e.g. `chcp 65001`), not the POSIX `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` env var; relying on the env-var path leaves `cmd.exe`/PowerShell 5.1 rendering agent box-drawing and emoji as mojibake.

title: Normalize BOTH sides before comparing paths from node-pty vs simple-git — separator mismatch silently falls back to the wrong worktree
summary: Worktree-ID inference during state hydration (`inferWorktreeIdFromCwd` in statePatcher.ts) longest-prefix-matches a node-pty `cwd` against simple-git worktree paths without normalizing separators; on Windows the mismatch silently falls back to `activeWorktreeId`, attaching restored panels to the wrong worktree with no error.

title: Interval-only crash backups lose data — add mutation triggers gated on a curated field set plus a focus-cancelling blur backup
summary: CrashRecoveryService's session-state.json backup relied solely on a 60s interval timer, so a crash between ticks restored stale state and lost panels created mid-setup; fix adds capture-on-change mutation triggers in handleAppSetState (gated to a curated field set) plus a blur backup on focus loss.

title: Crash-loop guards for utility-process hosts need a timestamp sliding window, NOT a reset-on-ready integer counter
summary: Utility-process host crash-loop guards (PtyHostLifecycle, WorkspaceHostProcess, MainProcessWatchdogClient): a reset-on-ready integer restart counter conflates fast and slow crash loops—instant pre-`markReady()` crashes trip the cap in milliseconds while hours-apart crashes are forgiven by each intervening ready and never accumulate; use a timestamp sliding window instead.

title: node-pty kill() signals the child but leaks the master fd — call destroy() (structurally), and gate pool refill with a per-key circuit breaker
summary: PtyPool (electron/services/PtyPool.ts) leaks the pty master fd on every pool-abandon path because node-pty kill() signals the child without closing /dev/ptmx; a misconfigured (cwd,envHash) whose warm shell exits on spawn triggers an unbounded spawn→exit→refill storm (~60 fds/iteration) toward the system fd limit. Fix: call destroy() structurally and gate refill with a per-key circuit breaker.

title: Ink-based agent TUIs (Copilot, Claude) need a submitEnterDelayMs GAP on interactive submit but a single-write quit — opposite timing for the same renderer
summary: Agent terminal input (PtyManager/terminalInput.ts) carries two opposed timing rules for the same Ink TUI renderer: interactive submit needs a `submitEnterDelayMs` gap between body and `\r`, while quit uses single-write; setting the delay to 0 (Copilot) makes Ink coalesce the keystrokes, silently freezing the input field after a delay—masquerading as a memory leak rather than a write-ordering bug.

title: Silent-fallback default on a destructive commit/push is a review blocker — gate on an explicitly authored message, never derive one
summary: Review Hub commit/push flow (`CommitPanel`/former `CommitComposerDialog`): deriving a commit subject via an `aiNote ?? lastCommitFirstLine` fallback silently reuses the previous commit's message, mislabeling unrelated staged files; gate submission on an explicitly authored message and preview the actual text, never a file count.

title: Node's global WebSocket silently drops custom request headers — use the `ws` package for header-authenticated WS endpoints (OpenAI realtime voice)
summary: Node 22+ ships a global `WebSocket`, but it silently strips custom upgrade headers (`Authorization`, `OpenAI-Beta`), so header-authenticated WS endpoints like OpenAI's realtime voice API fail as a spurious 401/immediate-close that mimics a bad token; use the `ws` package, which honors headers, for these connections in the Node main/utility process.

title: Every ResizeObserver-derived geometry consumer in the panel grid must gate on the sidebar layout-transition lock (not just the originally-patched one)
summary: Panel-grid ResizeObserver consumers that commit measured widths into inline or grid-template-column styles must all gate on the sidebar layout-transition lock (`layoutTransitionLock.ts`); `TwoPaneSplitLayout` was an unwired third consumer that re-snapped pane edges every frame during the 250ms slide, causing right-edge jitter on sidebar toggle.

title: --force-with-lease is unsafe with background fetches: pin the lease SHA at push-rejection time, not at click time
summary: Review Hub force-push recovery computes `--force-with-lease` against the current local remote-tracking ref, so Daintree's background `FetchScheduler` can advance `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` to the rejecting commits between rejection and click, making the lease silently match and degrade to an unsafe force push; pin the expected SHA at rejection time.

title: ESLint flat config is last-write-wins per rule: a new no-restricted-syntax block silently drops the global selectors for its files
summary: ESLint flat config (`eslint.config.js`, `tseslint.config`) applies `no-restricted-syntax` last-write-wins per rule, not merge-by-selector: adding a new narrowly-scoped block silently overrides and drops the global error-level selectors (IPC fire-and-forget, raw error.message in notify, CSP, Error-ternary) for those files with no warning or test failure.

title: Backgrounded terminal grid corruption from three compounding geometry bugs
summary: TerminalRendererPolicy/TerminalResizeController background-tier wake path corrupts the grid: deferred buffer reflow on demotion lets stale latestCols/latestRows and pixel-dedup lastWidth/lastHeight diverge, so the post-wake terminal.refresh() paints old glyphs into the new geometry; three individually-survivable geometry bugs compound, surfacing only under multi-worktree load.

title: Cross-store Zustand reads route through the storeAccessors leaf module; register accessors BEFORE the orchestrator idempotency guard so test re-init rebinds fresh singletons
summary: Renderer cross-store Zustand reads route through a `storeAccessors` leaf module; accessors must register before the orchestrator's idempotency guard or test `destroyStoreOrchestrator()` re-init leaves accessor closures and the fleetArming prune subscription bound to stale singletons, causing cross-test contamination plus boot-time TDZ crashes from inverted module evaluation order.

title: fs.watch({recursive:true}) leaks per-directory fds on macOS (EMFILE); @parcel/watcher uses one FSEvents stream per subtree + native ignore
summary: GitFileWatcher (electron/utils/gitFileWatcher.ts) uses Node fs.watch({recursive:true}) per worktree, which on macOS opens one fd per subdirectory and exhausts the workspace-host process's fd limit (EMFILE) under multi-worktree load, silently halting git-status events; @parcel/watcher fixes this by using a single FSEvents stream per subtree with native ignore filtering.

title: Don't materialize 'no user intent' into a concrete boolean — use tri-state pinned (true/false/undefined-follow-live) for toolbar visibility
summary: Toolbar agent-button visibility freezes after first launch because "no user intent" is materialized into a concrete boolean from a startup availability snapshot; CLI install/uninstall events stop propagating. Model pin state as tri-state (true/false/undefined-follow-live) so unpinned buttons keep tracking `cliAvailabilityStore`.

title: Cold WebContentsView project swap: keep outgoing view on top behind the incoming one until a renderer paint signal, not until did-finish-load
summary: ProjectViewManager cold WebContentsView project swaps flash a blank canvas because the old view is detached and the swap completes on `did-finish-load`, which fires before React's first commit; gate the outgoing-view teardown on an actual renderer paint signal instead.

title: xterm 6 clears the terminal selection synchronously in _keyDown for any PTY-forwarded key (including Escape)
summary: xterm 6 `Terminal._keyDown` synchronously clears the active selection on any PTY-forwarded key, including bare Escape, so terminal selection-gated features (`TerminalContextMenu` Copy enablement via `getSelection()`, copy-on-select, agent context injection branching on `hasSelection()`) silently lose the selection; also surfaces as flaky e2e when a helper presses Escape before right-clicking.

title: Strip a drag-gating CSS-transition class with flushSync before the first mousemove, and clear the parent's drag flag on unmount-mid-drag
summary: AppLayout sidebar/assistant panel drag-resize lags the pointer because the 250ms `ease-out-expo` `transition-[width]` keeps firing on every mousemove, easing toward each new width instead of tracking 1:1; gate the transition class off while `isResizing` and clear the parent's drag flag on unmount-mid-drag.

title: Env-keyed PTY pool: hash over the filtered view callers actually get, never raw options.env
summary: PtyPool (electron/services/PtyPool.ts) pre-warm pooling silently never serves agent launches because the `canUsePool` gate rejects any spawn carrying `options.env`, and every agent passes preset env vars; key the pool on a hash of the filtered env view callers actually receive, not raw `options.env`.

title: Electron net::ERR_* errors carry their signal only in err.message — a classifier reading err.code/statusCode/cause misclassifies every net blip as permanent
summary: AutoUpdaterService.isTransientUpdateError() walks the error cause chain inspecting Node-style err.code/statusCode, but electron-updater 6.3.x embeds Electron net::ERR_* signals only in err.message; the classifier never finds them, marks transient network blips as permanent, skips the retry backoff, and silently strands the user on a stale version.

title: PTY data-loss is a transient pulse, not a flow state — split TerminalFlowStatus into a PersistableFlowStatus subset and bypass status dedup at the drop site
summary: Terminal flow-status persistence: the `flowStatus` field on `PtyPanelData` doubles as live runtime signal and persisted panel state, so writing a transient PTY data-loss drop into it freezes `runtimeStatus` permanently (the instantaneous drop never clears) and collides with `BackpressureManager` status dedup; fix splits a `PersistableFlowStatus` subset and bypasses dedup at the drop site.

title: Multi-window view swaps break single-renderer assumptions: resolve active webContents at click-time, gate crash toasts on active-project match, add port-side close fallback
summary: ProjectViewManager multi-window architecture: code predating per-project WebContentsViews (#4672) captures `appWebContents` (the window shell) at dialog/handler-creation time, so "Restart view" crashes the wrong process and crash toasts fire for non-active cached views; resolve the active project webContents at click-time and gate notifications on active-project match.

title: A regressed stable latest-*.yml feed silently and permanently bricks auto-update — gate version monotonicity at publish time, fail-closed
summary: Auto-update publish pipeline (electron-updater stable channel, `allowDowngrade=false`): overwriting the live `latest-*.yml` feed with an equal-or-lower version permanently bricks update delivery on all installs, silently and client-irreversibly, until a strictly-greater version ships — back-merges resurfacing old versions are a common trigger; gate version monotonicity fail-closed at publish.

title: electron-store re-serializes the whole config on every set() — cap every persisted array through one shared writer, not per-path
summary: electron-store persistence (`electron/store.ts`) re-serializes the entire JSON config on every `set()`, so two independent writers of the `pendingErrors` array enforced inconsistent caps — the main-process fatal path appended uncapped while the renderer path capped at 50 — letting crash-loop errors grow the array unbounded and make each write progressively slower; route all persisted-array writes through one shared capped writer.

title: Crash-safe PTY reaping needs an OS-owned death channel, not cooperative cleanup or startup orphan sweeps
summary: Help-session PTY reaping in HelpSessionJobService leaks entire agent shell process trees when the main process dies hard (crash, force-quit, OOM): cooperative kill and the persisted-PID startup orphan sweep both assume an orderly exit or a follow-up relaunch, so an OS-owned death channel is required — and on macOS each orphan also exhausts one of ~511 system PTY fds.

title: MCP side-effecting tools need two-window idempotency: singleflight + success-only TTL cache, cleared on session drain
summary: MCP side-effecting tool dispatch (`sessionServer.ts` `CallToolRequestSchema`) needs dual-window idempotency: an in-flight singleflight Promise map catches concurrent duplicates while a success-only TTL result cache catches sequential ones; caching failures pins transient errors for the TTL, and the cache must be cleared on session drain so stale post-drain resolutions don't leak.

title: Non-atomic recursive fs.cp of the help template: gate with a content-hash stamp, not app version — and re-do side effects the skipped copy used to perform
summary: HelpSessionService.provisionSession recopies the bundled help/ template via non-atomic fs.cp on every launch; a mid-copy crash leaves a torn session dir reused next launch. Gate the copy on a content-hash stamp (not app version), and re-run any side effects the skipped copy previously performed.

title: BrowserWindow.destroy() synchronously fires window-all-closed — destroy-then-recreate quits the app mid-flight; guard with a counter, not a boolean
summary: Electron window recreation (`createWindow.ts`, `ProjectViewManager`): destroying a `BrowserWindow` synchronously fires `window-all-closed`, so a boolean "recreating" guard set after `destroy()` arrives too late and `app.quit()` runs mid-recreate; use an increment/decrement pending-window counter instead.

title: Renderer fire-and-forget kill IPC can't enforce a single-backend PTY invariant — the main process must displace priors at provision time
summary: HelpSessionService's main-process single-backend PTY invariant (one assistant backend per project) can't be enforced by renderer fire-and-forget kill IPC; a dropped/raced/crashed teardown leaves an orphan PTY dispatching MCP tool calls under a still-valid bearer, so re-provision must displace priors server-side.

title: 'ConfirmDialog typed-name gate (D3): `?? ""` preserves an empty string that strict-equals empty input and silently clears the gate — use `||` and constrain the target by variant'
summary: ConfirmDialog typed-name gate (`typedNameTarget`/`TypedNameConfirmInput`) for D3 destructive actions silently disarms when the target resolves to an empty string: `worktree.branch ?? worktree.name` keeps `""` for detached-HEAD/branchless worktrees, making `"" === ""` true on open. Use `||` not `??`, and constrain the target per variant.

title: Bulk WebGL attaches blank terminals for 3s — stagger via rAF, pre-empt xterm's restore timer in capture phase, and loseContext() to free the slot
summary: TerminalWebGLManager bulk-attach race: Chromium's 16-WebGL-context-per-renderer cap evicts the oldest contexts when many agent terminals call ensureContext() in the same frame during bulk worktree creation, leaving terminals blank ~3s; fix staggers attaches via rAF, pre-empts xterm's restore timer in the capture phase, and calls loseContext() to free slots.

title: A hook needing only a constant pulled @xterm/addon-webgl into the eager renderer chunk — split static config from the heavy module and lazy-import behind a synchronous pending-replay queue
summary: Renderer boot eagerly fetches and parses the ~33KB-gzip `@xterm/addon-webgl` because `TerminalWebGLManager` statically imports the addon alongside a pool-size constant consumed by `useResourceProfile` on the critical path; a sibling constant import silently drags the whole heavy module into the eager chunk graph.

title: xterm cursorBlink runs a per-pane setInterval regardless of focus, and every terminal.options.scrollback write rebuilds the CircularList — both need central re-clamping under tier oscillation
summary: TerminalInstanceService refresh-tier ladder leaks two per-pane costs in background xterm 6.0 panes: cursorBlink's CursorBlinkStateManager setInterval fires on all visible (not just focused) panes, and each scrollback write rebuilds the CircularList, so rapid tab-flipping thrashes the buffer with GC pressure; both need central re-clamping in onTierApplied.

title: Focus-tiered git watcher: asymmetric hysteresis on rotation, and a cooldown branch that sets a pending flag but arms no drain timer defers events to the next 60-300s poll
summary: WatcherController (electron/workspace-host/WatcherController.ts) focus-tiered git watcher: rapid worktree focus flips synchronously tear down and re-arm the recursive @parcel/watcher, churning per-directory inotify watches on Linux and risking ENOSPC; separately, the self-trigger cooldown branch sets gitWatchRefreshPending and returns without arming a drain timer, so an isolated .git/ event in the cooldown window is deferred to the next 60-300s poll.

title: xterm 6.0 ships Unicode 6 widths by default — load addon-unicode11 in BOTH the renderer terminal and the headless analyzer terminal, or emoji/CJK mis-measure and corrupt agent-state detection
summary: xterm 6.0 defaults to Unicode 6 cell widths, so emoji and CJK glyphs measure as one cell instead of two unless `@xterm/addon-unicode11` is loaded; the headless `SynchronizedFrameAnalyzer` terminal in `TerminalProcess` needs the addon too, or per-column `cell.width` tracking drifts and silently corrupts agent-state detection rather than just glitching the visible TUI.

title: SQLite corruption probe: PRAGMA schema_version is a no-op that 'succeeds' on corrupt files — use quick_check, and foreign_keys is per-connection off-by-default
summary: SQLite startup corruption probe (`probeDb` in `electron/services/persistence/db.ts`) gives false confidence: `PRAGMA schema_version` is a no-op that returns success on corrupt files (use `quick_check`), extended corruption codes like `SQLITE_CORRUPT_INDEX` bypass the classifier, and `foreign_keys` is per-connection and off by default so FK clauses go silently unenforced.

title: Panel-kind registry: guard built-in entries by extensionId absence, not a kind-string allowlist; reject overwrites without churning the useSyncExternalStore snapshot
summary: Panel-kind registry (`PANEL_KIND_REGISTRY` / `PANEL_KIND_DEFINITION_REGISTRY`) lets plugins hijack built-in kinds by re-registering the same id string; guard built-ins by absence of `extensionId` rather than a hardcoded kind-string allowlist that silently rots when new built-ins are added, and reject overwrites without churning the useSyncExternalStore snapshot.

title: Zustand v5 persist runs migrate() only on a numeric version mismatch — sanitize/clean existing persisted blobs in merge(), not migrate()
summary: Zustand v5 persist store sanitization: migrate() fires only on numeric version mismatch, so pre-version blobs (no version field) and blobs already at the target version skip it entirely — clean existing persisted data in merge() instead, which runs on every rehydration regardless of version.

title: Sentry crash capture: drain the async transport before app.exit, and scrub stack-frame source/vars not just filename
summary: Sentry crash telemetry in the Electron main process loses production crash reports because the fatal `uncaughtException` handler calls synchronous `app.exit(1)` before the async HTTP transport can flush in-flight envelopes; separately, `sanitizeEvent`'s `beforeSend` frame scrubbing only walks filename/abs_path, leaking PII in `context_line`, `pre_context`, `post_context`, and `vars`.

title: useSyncExternalStore for reading a mutable singleton service into render — getSnapshot must return a primitive or a cached reference, never a fresh object
summary: KeybindingService keybinding-display hooks (useEffectiveCombo/useKeybindingDisplay) read a mutable non-React singleton via useState+useEffect-subscribe, which tears under React 19 concurrent rendering when a rebind mutates mid-render; use useSyncExternalStore with a getSnapshot returning a primitive or cached reference, never a fresh object, to avoid infinite re-render loops.

title: Write-only SQLite transactions must pass behavior:'immediate' — drizzle's DEFERRED default deadlocks under a parallel WAL reader with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT
summary: Main-process WAL SQLite persistence (db.ts/ProjectStore/ScratchStore): write-only drizzle transactions must pass behavior:'immediate' because the DEFERRED default fails with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT under a parallel reader (readLastProjectId.ts), which busy_timeout cannot retry.

title: Store migrations are non-atomic with their version bump — every migration must be replay-safe, and shipped Drizzle .sql files are immutable
summary: Boot-time store migrations run non-atomically: a migration body that completes before its version bump is persisted re-runs on next boot, causing fatal `table already exists` crashes (Drizzle .sql replay) or silent overwrites of user-changed settings/pinned agents; migrations must be idempotent and shipped .sql files immutable.

title: Crash-marker write timing: mark clean exit only AFTER the cleanup chain settles, and never record a crash for a non-fatal unhandledRejection
summary: CrashRecoveryService exit-cleanliness classification mistimes its on-disk crash marker (running.lock): clean-exit is recorded before the before-quit cleanup chain settles—so a 10s-hard-timeout app.exit(1) reads as clean—and a non-fatal unhandledRejection calls recordCrash(), making the next normal Cmd-Q boot as a phantom crash.

title: MCP auth: two independent Bearer-header parsers diverged and silently dropped tokens to workbench tier
summary: MCP server tier authorization (`tierAuth.ts`) duplicates Bearer-header parsing across `isAuthorized` and `resolveTokenTier`; when the two parsers diverge (e.g. TAB vs space scheme separator), a token can authenticate yet silently demote to the lowest `workbench` tier, stripping privileges with no error surfaced.

title: Main-process signal handler: safety-belt timer must outlast the cleanup budget, dev signals must route through before-quit, and a one-shot guard must keep a force-exit escape hatch
summary: Main-process signal handler in `electron/lifecycle/appLifecycle.ts` mishandles graceful shutdown: a 5s safety-belt timer undercuts the 10s cleanup budget and kills the process mid-cleanup, while unregistered SIGHUP (dev terminal close) bypasses `before-quit` entirely, so `markCleanExit()` and telemetry flush never run and CrashLoopGuard misfires on next launch.

title: Hardening IPC git argv: --no-ext-diff isn't enough (need --no-textconv + cat-file), and --end-of-options doesn't protect range tokens
summary: GitService and WorkspaceService IPC git argv hardening: renderer-supplied refs, worktree paths, and diff ranges flow unvalidated into `git.raw`/`git.diff`, where leading-dash values are parsed as flags (`--upload-pack`), `--no-ext-diff` still permits `.gitattributes` textconv/smudge filters to execute arbitrary binaries during read-side diff/show, and `--end-of-options` fails to protect range tokens — requiring `--no-textconv`, cat-file blob reads, and per-arg dash guards.

title: Classify GitHub errors by Octokit typed-dispatch (instanceof + .status/.response.headers), not error.message substring matching
summary: GitHub error classification (`parseGitHubError` in GitHubErrors.ts feeding `isTokenRelatedError`/`isTransientNetworkError`) misclassifies transient incidents — 5xx, DNS blips, HTML-page 401s from the auth service, and `X-GitHub-SSO: partial-results` headers — as token-invalid because it pattern-matches `error.message` substrings instead of Octokit's typed `instanceof` plus `.status`/`.response.headers`, surfacing false reconnect banners during outages.

title: Hardened simple-git factories: GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS/--no-write-fetch-head stop side-effect writes, and .env() replaces wholesale so wrapping factories must re-state every flag
summary: simple-git hardening in electron/utils/hardenedGit.ts: background status/log polling and fetch silently write the repo (index.lock stat-cache refresh, FETCH_HEAD), contending with foreground terminal git; credential-helper ops can hang on hidden interactive prompts. Fix via GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS/--no-write-fetch-head and disabled prompting — but simple-git's .env() replaces the environment wholesale, so wrapping factories must re-state every inherited flag or silently lose hardening.

title: Version-header opaque persisted blobs whose format is owned by an external library (xterm addon-serialize .restore files)
summary: Terminal scrollback persistence (`terminalSessionPersistence.ts`) writes raw `SerializeAddon.serialize()` output to `.restore` files as an undeclared schema; when `@xterm/addon-serialize` changes its format across a version bump, old blobs replay into silently scrambled scrollback with no error, since nothing distinguishes the writer's format from the reader's.

title: Soft-reset the headless xterm parser before replaying a serialized session — content replay does not clear leaked DEC private modes, and DECSTR alone misses Kitty keyboard + cursor style
summary: Terminal session persistence (`restoreSessionFromFile` in `terminalSessionPersistence.ts`): replaying a serialized `@xterm/headless` snapshot leaks DEC private modes across hibernate/restore, since content replay never clears them and DECSTR alone misses Kitty keyboard protocol and cursor style — restored terminals behave as if still inside the prior alt-screen TUI. Soft-reset the parser before replay.

title: PTY queue managers: clearQueue must self-release its own coordinator token AND drop stale byte accounting before force-resuming
